claim: The F4c MISMATCH measured on windows-latest was a harness line-ending defect, NOT a divergence of the Zig core: the case manifest was written in text mode, so its \r\n separators left a 0x0d at the end of the stdin field and the Zig core was handed input it should not have had.

event.harness (windows-latest): completed failure (job 117618400798): F4c ran for real this time -- vendored oracle hash matched the pin, so the .gitattributes fix of entry 26 worked -- and the gate then reported MISMATCH, exit 1

measured_counts_on_windows.all_four_are: side=zig, the empty-stdin EOF cases; every fed-input case matched
measured_counts_on_windows.python_side: matched the oracle in all 10 cases, which localises the defect to the path that feeds the Zig driver, not to Classic semantics

mechanism:
evidence/compare_f4_canonical.py built evidence/_f4c_cases.tsv with Path.write_text(), which on Windows translates 
 to 
. evidence/run_f4c.zig splits the manifest on '
' only, so each line kept a trailing CR on its LAST field -- the stdin field. A case declared with empty stdin therefore reached the core as one byte 0x0d (13), and the machine echoed 13 instead of taking the canonical EOF branch (3^10-1 = 59048 -> out 0xa8). Cases with fed input matched because their programs consume fewer bytes than the CR-padded field holds.

reproduced_locally.method: A/B on this machine, no Windows needed: the pre-fix driver (git show HEAD:evidence/run_f4c.zig) and the post-fix driver, each fed the same three EOF cases through a LF manifest and through a CRLF manifest
reproduced_locally.identity_with_ci: those three hashes are byte-for-byte the 'got' values in the windows-latest report, so the explanation is measured, not inferred
reproduced_locally.old_driver_with_LF_manifest: identical to the post-fix rows below (the leak needs the CRLF manifest)
reproduced_locally.expected_side_reference: the post-fix hashes equal the canonical oracle's expected hashes recorded in the windows report, i.e. the Zig core now agrees with the oracle on both manifest flavours

fix.evidence/compare_f4_canonical.py: manifest written with write_bytes(...encode('utf-8')) instead of write_text(), so the separator is LF on every platform
fix.evidence/run_f4c.zig: each manifest line is trimEnd(u8, line, "\\r")'d before parsing, so a CRLF manifest cannot inject 0x0d into stdin even if one appears
fix.why_both: the writer fixes this gate; the reader fixes the class of mistake. Only the writer change would leave the driver fragile, and only the reader change would leave a manifest whose declared stdin is a lie

local_remeasurement_after_fix.verdict_line: => PASS (11 cases x 2 cores x 2 oracle(s) = 44 stdout-hash comparisons)
local_remeasurement_after_fix.note: Linux was never affected (its text-mode write is LF), so this fix is invisible locally -- which is exactly why it needed the Windows runner to surface.

not_rewritten: the entry-25 and entry-26 artifacts keep their published bytes; the earlier reports were correct measurements of what each side actually received, including the wrong 0x0d input.
scope: the F4c harness plumbing on windows-latest. Nothing about Classic semantics changed: src/malbolge_free.zig and src/malbolge_core.py are untouched and still hash to the entry-24 seals.
not_claimed: Windows CI green is not claimed here. This file records the diagnosis and the fix; the run that decides it is verified with gh run watch --exit-status and reported in the ledger.
why_it_matters: a parity verdict is only about the machine under test if the input it received is the input the case declares. A CR smuggled in by a line-ending default turned a correct core into a 'mismatch', and the honest reading of that is a bug in the harness -- not a licence to touch the core.
